title: Quantum Dot Moiré from Crossed MoS2 Nanoribbons
authors: Xinting Shuai, Hao Zhang, Wenjing Wu, Chongning Wu, Maryam Amiri, T. A. M. Ragib Shahriar, Dian Pan, Zhi Kai Ng, Tymofii Pieshkov, Leeza Dutta, Yijun Zhou, Rohith Narra, Luke Van Leeuwen, Jishnu Murukeshan, Luyao Shi, Jiawei Lai, Atin Pramanik, Bipin Kumar Gupta, Edwin Hang Tong Teo, Robert Vajtai, Xiang Zhang, Hanyu Zhu, Shengxi Huang, Aditya D. Mohite, Pulickel M. Ajayan
abstract: Twisted atomically thin layers have attracted much attention for Moiré potential and correlated quantum phenomena. However, existing Moiré superlattices have largely been limited to extensive wavefunction without lateral confinement. Here we introduce a new platform where 1D nanoribbons of 2D MoS2 grown by vapor deposition can be easily superposed at various angles from stacking and transferring, to form Moiré quantum dots at their intersections with unique exciton physics. Angle-dependent Moiré intersections show enhanced exciton emission at commensurate angle 22 deg, which demonstrates faster relaxation at the cryogenic temperature. A size-dependent study further exhibits a reduced exciton energy and soften out-of-plane interlayer coupling for smaller Moiré areas. Our results reveal exciton physics turnability via precise overlapping of 1D nanoribbons.
summary: The research introduces a novel platform using stacked 1D $	ext{MoS}_2$ nanoribbons to create Moiré Quantum Dots (MQDs). By controlling the overlap angle and size, the authors demonstrate that the resulting exciton physics is highly tunable. This work advances the study of moiré phenomena by confining them to discrete quantum dot junctions.
main_problem: To study Moiré physics in a confined geometry, moving beyond the limitations of extended 2D-2D twisted bilayers which lack intrinsic lateral confinement.
main_result: The authors demonstrated that precise overlapping of 1D $	ext{MoS}_2$ nanoribbons forms Moiré quantum dots (MQDs) whose exciton physics is tunable by controlling the overlap angle and size.
method: The study involves synthesizing and deterministically stacking monolayer $	ext{MoS}_2$ nanoribbons using CVD growth followed by controlled transfer and annealing onto a substrate.
model_or_system: The physical system is Moiré Quantum Dots (MQDs) formed at the intersection of stacked 1D $	ext{MoS}_2$ nanoribbons, creating a quasi-0D quantum dot structure with tunable moiré potentials.
key_observables: Angle-dependent exciton emission (enhanced at $22^\circ$), PL redshift dependent on size, and temperature-dependent fast radiative channels.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), Moiré dot size, cryogenic temperature regime.
main_assumptions: The system is treated as a quasi-0D quantum-dot system due to the 1D building blocks; edge-mediated lattice reconstruction deepens the local Moiré potential.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the fabrication process (SEM images of NRs, OM image of stacked MQDs) and atomic schematics confirming the stacking geometry and resulting Moiré pattern.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure detailing synthesis (CVD growth of 1D NRs), assembly (controlled stacking/transfer), and characterization using PL and structural microscopy to observe angle-dependent electronic properties.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental realization of highly confined, tunable moiré systems, allowing for the study of quantum phenomena in a controlled, quasi-zero-dimensional geometry relevant to solid-state quantum emitters.
